currentState.persistence: Existing owner rows are durable and can be listed, paused, or deleted; new creation and paused-task resume/retry fail before persistence because availability is hard-coded false.
currentState.database: scheduled_tasks, scheduled_task_runs, notification delivery tables, owner RLS, and service-role claim/recovery/settlement RPCs exist.
currentState.engine: A dormant secret-protected HTTP ingress and sequential database-leased AI execution batch exist at source level.
currentState.ui: Paid owners see truthful unavailable messaging, historical task rows, pause/delete, and disabled resume/retry; creation and Automation Builder are hidden.
currentState.cloudflareRole: Existing edge/web deployment only; no approved scheduling role.
currentState.lovableDependency: No Lovable runtime or service is part of the proposed execution path.

rootBlockers: No Azure timer, Container Apps Job, Function, queue dispatcher, or deployed worker invokes the dormant engine.
scheduledExecutionAvailable is hard-coded false, intentionally blocking creation and resume.
Azure Bicep provisions the web Container App only and does not wire scheduler identity, secrets, job policy, or alerts.
Claim and run-start persistence are split, retries overwrite one occurrence history row, and leases have no heartbeat.
Direct authenticated task UPDATE/DELETE permits unsafe execution-state and cancellation races.
Entitlement is not rechecked atomically at claim and scheduled use is not proven to share canonical AI cost accounting.
Recurrence stores an instant plus coarse repeat value, not an IANA-zone wall-clock rule; DST is not production-safe.
Availability readiness checks credentials rather than a fresh successful scheduler heartbeat.

chosenArchitecture.trigger: Azure Container Apps scheduled Job every minute in UTC
chosenArchitecture.compute: Dedicated non-HTTP scheduled-worker image built from this repository and pinned by immutable ACR digest
chosenArchitecture.state: Supabase Postgres is authoritative for owners, schedules, entitlements-at-claim, occurrences, attempts, leases, settlement, outbox, and RLS
chosenArchitecture.identity: Azure managed identity for ACR, Key Vault, Azure OpenAI, and monitoring; worker-only Supabase service credential from Key Vault
chosenArchitecture.observability: Container Apps logs plus Log Analytics and Application Insights metrics/alerts, with a Supabase heartbeat used for product availability
chosenArchitecture.executionModel: At-least-once claims with transactional occurrence/attempt idempotency, lease heartbeat, bounded pool, atomic settlement, and read-only prompts
chosenArchitecture.cloudflare: DNS/approved edge only; no triggering or execution
chosenArchitecture.rationale: It reuses existing Container Apps, ACR, identity, Key Vault, Azure OpenAI, Log Analytics, and Application Insights while avoiding a redundant broker and public HTTP scheduler dependency.

alternativesRejected.name: Azure Functions timer
alternativesRejected.reason: Adds Function host, storage account, packaging, and deployment machinery absent from the repo; database idempotency is still required.

alternativesRejected.name: Azure Service Bus
alternativesRejected.reason: Requires dispatcher, namespace/queue, consumer, outbox publishing, and reconciliation while Supabase already provides the durable due queue; reserve for measured fan-out needs.

alternativesRejected.name: Azure Storage Queues
alternativesRejected.reason: Still adds dual-system dispatch and poison/reconciliation logic with fewer controls than Service Bus and no current scale justification.

alternativesRejected.name: Always-on Container App
alternativesRejected.reason: Adds polling leadership and idle compute; a finite scheduled Job matches the current batch.

alternativesRejected.name: Supabase pg_cron or Edge Functions
alternativesRejected.reason: Conflicts with the finalized Azure execution and observability boundary.

alternativesRejected.name: Cloudflare Cron
alternativesRejected.reason: Cloudflare is restricted to approved DNS/edge responsibilities and must not execute scheduled work.

alternativesRejected.name: Production HTTP bearer invocation
alternativesRejected.reason: Depends on public web ingress and a shared secret; direct non-HTTP Job execution is smaller in trust surface.

uiChanges: Enable authoring/resume only when the backend proves a fresh scheduler heartbeat.
Add timezone-aware create/edit recurrence controls and document DST policy.

securityRequirements: No public worker ingress, Cloudflare execution, or Lovable runtime/service dependency.
Worker secrets only in Key Vault references; never browser variables, image layers, logs, arguments, outputs, or artifacts.
Service-role RPCs verify role and opaque lease token, pin search_path, bound inputs, and revoke public/anon/authenticated execution.
Owner RPCs derive auth.uid and never accept owner identity; explicit owner SELECT RLS and composite ownership constraints remain.
Restrict initial scheduled tasks to model generation/read-only behavior until side-effect tools have authorization and idempotency contracts.
Never log prompt, result, raw user ID, email, provider body, auth header, or secret; use keyed pseudonymous identifiers.
Recheck entitlement/quota at claim and account for usage atomically.
Run strict zero-Lovable and artifact secret scans before release.

Oldest due age, claim latency, execution duration percentiles, active/expired/recovered leases, and settlement conflicts.
Outbox depth/age and delivery result metrics.
Alerts for heartbeat age, lag, consecutive Job failures, lease expiry, terminal failure rate, provider errors, delivery lag, and budget.
Authorized readiness exposes only safe capability state; scheduler outage degrades Scheduled Tasks, not web liveness.

Recurrence golden tests for zones, DST gap/fold, month end, leap year, invalid zones, and edits.
Concurrent claim, overlap, ordering, fairness, lease heartbeat/recovery, stale token, and cancellation race tests.
Idempotent claim/heartbeat/settlement/outbox replay and crash-boundary fault injection.
Retry classification, backoff/jitter/Retry-After, max attempts, and missed-run coalescing tests.
Entitlement, plan-limit, quota accounting, downgrade-at-claim, and refund tests.
Two-user RLS, forged identity, direct mutation denial, worker RPC denial, and secret/log redaction tests.
UI unavailable/degraded/ready, lifecycle/history, accessibility, responsive, and truthful-error tests.
Bicep lint/build/what-if and identity, secret, no-ingress, cron, limits, digest, logs, alerts tests.
Seven-day isolated staging soak plus rollback drill with zero duplicates and zero cross-user access.
Existing typecheck, lint, build, unit, integration, API, release, migration, and strict zero-Lovable suites.
rolloutPlan: Phase 1: expand schema/RPC/RLS contracts and disable-backed legacy migration.
Phase 2: implement worker, recurrence, entitlement/accounting, heartbeat, outbox, and telemetry behind flag off.
Phase 3: provision Azure staging Job/image/identity/logging/alerts only.
Phase 4: isolated fault-injected staging verification and minimum seven-day soak.
Phase 5: ship UI and controlled internal/small paid cohort enablement gated by heartbeat.
Phase 6: protected production readiness/canary, gradual enablement, runbooks, and later v1 contract cleanup.
rollbackPlan: Turn off the server-side execution flag so create/resume fail closed.
Suspend the Azure scheduled Job without deleting it.
Request cancellation, wait a lease window, and use audited recovery rather than blanket status reset.
Roll worker/web to prior immutable ACR digests while retaining expand-only schema.
Disable outbox drain independently if notification delivery is faulty.
Preserve history/logs, reconcile occurrences with an approved script, and rotate suspected credentials.
Success requires no new claims/live leases/duplicates, owner isolation, web availability, and truthful unavailable UI.
